generation.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Electric Power Monthly (Form EIA-923), net generation by state and source, grouped by the ERW (docs/methods/generation_mix.md)
generation.hourly_reason: No public source gives a state's generation by the hour; the hourly picture is by balancing authority, in the Grid tool.

retail.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-861M, retail sales and average price by state and sector
retail.revenue_note: Revenue is EIA's sales times EIA's average price for the same month and sector. EIA computes its average price as revenue over sales, so the product gives EIA's revenue to within the price's rounding (one tenth of a dollar a MWh).

plants.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory (Form EIA-860M)
plants.unit: MW (nameplate and net summer); MWh (storage energy)
plants.retired_note: EIA-860M's retired sheet as the ERW's table holds it: the generators retired in its window, not every retirement since 2001.

co2.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, emissions by state by fuel
co2.unit: metric tons of CO2; kg of CO2 per MWh

gas.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Natural Gas Monthly, consumption by end use and production by state
gas.production_reason: EIA prints no marketed production for Minnesota: it is not a producing state in the Natural Gas Monthly

energy.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Energy Data System

by_sector_reason.commercial: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the commercial sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy
by_sector_reason.transportation: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the transportation sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy

disposition.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, source and disposition
disposition.note: Net interstate trade is EIA's figure: positive where the state took in more electricity from other states than it sent out.

serving.source: U.S. Census Bureau county population estimates, and Form EIA-861's utilities and balancing authorities by county, as the ERW's table eia_county_region joins them

by_authority.reason: its utilities name no balancing authority in EIA-861's sales file

serving.basis: Each county counts once, whole, for its primary authority: the one whose utilities serve most of the county's customers in EIA-861. A county two authorities share is counted for its primary one.

large_load_laws.source: The ERW's large-load research files, each law read at its legislature's or regulator's own page

laws.bill: H.F. No. 16 (Laws 2025, First Special Session, chapter 12)
laws.title: relating to data centers; modifying various environmental and energy regulatory requirements governing data centers; authorizing a clean energy and capacity tariff; modifying sales and use tax exemptions; imposing a fee
laws.threshold: no MW figure for the very large customer class: the Commission defines it for each utility by order by 15 December 2026; a data center is defined as a facility designed to have a load of 100 MW or more; the qualified large-scale data center fee starts at 100 MW of peak demand
laws.requirements: commission rulemaking: the Commission must establish by order, by 15 December 2026, the definition and characteristics of a very large customer class or subclass for each public utility, in a rate case or another proceeding; it may approve, modify or reject a tariff or electric service agreement between a utility and a very large customer [p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 1: "The commission may do this in a rate case under section 216B.16 for that utility or in another proceeding." | p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 2: "The commission may approve, modify or reject a tariff or electric service agreement proposed between a public utility and a very large customer establishing the terms and conditions under which the utility will provide electric service to the customer."] || cost allocation: the Commission must consider how best to achieve that all costs attributable to very large customers not exempt are assigned to the very large customer class or subclass [p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 2(1): "(1) all costs attributable to the utility's very large customers not exempt under subdivision 3 are assigned to the very large customer class or subclass determined by the commission under paragraph (a);"] || exit fee: no exit fee printed: the tariff or agreement must contain protections so other customers are not placed at risk for paying stranded costs of serving the very large customer [p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 2(3): "(3) the tariff or agreement contains protections necessary to ensure that other customers of the public utility are not placed at risk for paying stranded costs associated with the utility serving the very large customer; and"] || other: the electricity provided to a very large customer must achieve each benchmark of the state's electricity standards (216B.1691), shown by a utility plan to serve the load without asking to delay or modify the standards; existing, renewed or extended agreements and very large customers taking service before 2020 are exempt [p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 2(2): "(2) the electricity to be provided by the utility to a very large customer achieves each quantitative benchmark of the state's electricity standards under section 216B.1691" | p. 1, 216B.1622 subd. 3: "This section shall not apply to existing, renewed, or extended electric service agreements of public utility customers meeting the threshold of a very large customer, or to very large customers that have been actively taking electric service from the public utility prior to 2020."] || other: an annual fee the commissioner collects from each qualified large-scale data center, by the peak demand the utility arranges to serve: 2,000,000 dollars for 100 to 250 MW up to 5,000,000 dollars for 750 MW or more, paid into the energy and conservation account [p. 1, 216B.72(a): "(a) The commissioner must collect an annual fee from the qualified large-scale data center, on a schedule prescribed by the commissioner and deposited in the energy and conservation account established in section 216B.241, subdivision 2a." | p. 1, 216B.72(b)(1): "$2,000,000" | p. 1, 216B.72(b)(4): "(4) 750 MW or greater" | p. 1, 216B.72(b)(4): "$5,000,000"] || other: each public utility must offer an optional clean energy and capacity tariff for commercial and industrial customers by special contract, with participants paying all proportional costs of the new resources and no cost shifting either way [p. 1, Sec. 10, 216B.1623: "The commission shall require each public utility to offer a clean energy and capacity tariff for commercial and industrial customers." | p. 1, 216B.1623(5): "(5) prohibit cost shifting from the participating customers to other utility customers or vice versa; and"]

severance.reason: the severance tool holds Texas, Louisiana, New Mexico only
